title: SOLID: single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution

videos.script: Five letters, and this lesson takes the first three. {{title}} A principle is not a law. It is a guess about where the next change will hurt, written down by people who were hurt by it. {{guess}} Single responsibility asks who will ask for a change. You will watch the fines office change how days are counted, and the statistics team's average drop with it. Nobody on that team touched a line. {{actors}} Then a report with three owners, split so that each request lands in one place. {{split}} Open and closed asks whether a new case means editing working code. A chain of ifs prints a receipt for none cents. A protocol and a table of rules take a new fine without opening the old files. {{open}} Liskov substitution asks whether a child keeps its parent's promises. A reference book that refuses to be lent. A laptop due back the day it went out. A square that moves both sides when you set one. {{promises}} Each of them matches its parent's signature, and each of them breaks a caller. At the end, one test written for the parent, run against every child, catches all three. {{contract}}
